findings.description: eval() dynamically evaluates Python expressions and can execute attacker-controlled code.
findings.recommendation: Avoid eval(). Use explicit parsing, validation, or an allow-list of supported operations.

findings.description: os.system() executes operating-system commands and may become vulnerable when input is attacker-controlled.
findings.recommendation: Avoid os.system(). Prefer subprocess with shell=False and validate command arguments.

findings.description: Subprocess execution can become dangerous when command arguments originate from untrusted input.
findings.recommendation: Use shell=False and pass arguments as a list. Validate externally supplied arguments.

findings.description: pickle deserialization can execute arbitrary code when processing malicious data.
findings.recommendation: Never deserialize untrusted pickle data. Prefer JSON or another safe serialization format.
